instrument.title: When a person attains an age, for a written law that does not fix the rule itself
instrument.provision: the general rule (common law or a decided case) that applies to Acts with no age-reckoning clause of their own

question: A person is born on 14 March 2003. On what date, and at what moment, does she attain the age of 21 for the purposes of an Act that has no age-reckoning clause of its own, such as the Parliamentary Elections Act 1954, the Human Organ Transplant Act 1987 or the Wills Act 1838?

trigger.act: turned 21: became an elector, a presumed organ donor, and able to make a will and a lasting power of attorney

expected.assertion: not known: either the anniversary (as seven Acts provide for themselves) or an earlier common-law moment; to be taken from a decided case, not assumed

assumption.text: the anniversary of birth, at the start of the day

attach_to.note: A doctrine with no statute. Once settled, every row whose Act lacks its own clause should read its ages from it. Seven deposited Acts state the anniversary rule for themselves (Women's Charter, CPF, CareShield Life, MediShield Life, Child Development Co-Savings, Children and Young Persons, Social Residential Homes); those rows can encode their own clause instead.

closes_when.text: Every age-gated event in Simone's replay that arises under an Act without its own age clause takes its age from an encoded, cited rule.

notes: Split from REQ-0013, which asked the Interpretation Act 1965; that Act has no provision on attaining an age (see subjects/sg/interpretation-act/encodings/naive-2026-10/NOTES.md). count carries REQ-0013's three occurrences.
